slides.notes:
The question and the data
Sleep staging from one EEG channel
Sleep staging assigns a label to each 30-second EEG epoch across a recorded night.
We present a simpler CNN + BiGRU study, not a replication of the original paper.
Conceptual EEG scene. The trace is illustrative, not a recorded signal.

The evaluated cohort
The evaluated subset contains 20 participants and 39 nights, with 42,307 retained epochs.
Participant separation matters because different nights from the same person are related.
Each figure represents one participant. Counts come from the archived closeout.

Five sleep-stage labels
The model predicts one of five labels. We evaluate every class, not only overall accuracy.
Macro-F1 gives each class equal weight. Accuracy counts all correctly classified epochs.
Stage colors identify categories. The animated timeline is illustrative.

Subject-wise evaluation
Each fold separates participants into training, validation and test sets without subject overlap.
Only two participants form each test fold. Small fold samples create substantial variability.
Subject-wise protocol differs from the paper; test < 10 subjects per fold (20 total)

How the model reads a night
EEG becomes a time-frequency image
The short-time Fourier transform describes how frequency content changes within each EEG epoch.
The resulting log-spectrogram has 129 frequency bins and 29 time bins.
The example trace and spectrogram illustrate the transform. They are not measured data.

The CNN encodes each epoch
The CNN extracts local time-frequency patterns and compresses each epoch into a feature vector.
These are conceptual feature blocks. Their colors do not represent learned activations.
Architecture from src/model.py. Feature maps and filters are conceptual.

BiGRU adds within-night context
A bidirectional GRU reads the sequence in both directions and combines neighboring context.
Sequences stay within a single night. Bidirectional context makes this an offline model.
Illustrative sequence. Connections show architecture, not estimated causal effects.

One inference path for validation and test
Validation and test use the same sliding-window inference path with stride five.
Evaluation mode disables dropout and uses saved BatchNorm statistics. Windows never cross nights.
Window placement is illustrative. The stride and averaging rule come from the code.

The normalization intervention
The baseline failed on specific nights
The baseline had severe errors on particular nights, including one night predicted entirely as wakefulness.
Four diagnostic rounds found no confirmed pairing, timing, channel or label-alignment defect.
Archived test results informed this diagnosis. Later R1 selection was post-hoc.

R1 changes the normalization rule
R1 standardizes every frequency bin using the retained epochs of that same night.
R1 is post-hoc and transductive. Retraining plus normalization prevents a model-only causal claim.
R1 uses retained epochs whose selection includes hypnogram-based trimming. Waves are illustrative.

Archived results improved with R1
Subject-mean macro-F1 rose from 56.42% to 74.86%. Pooled accuracy rose from 65.00% to 80.99%.
The comparison combines changed normalization with retrained weights and access to unlabeled test-night signals.
Historical test results. R1 and full-night sensitivity use offline, transductive normalization.

Sensitivity uses the complete PSG signal
The sensitivity run computes statistics across the complete signal without labels selecting the normalization range.
It scores 71.84% macro-F1. It still uses each evaluation night's unlabeled signal and remains transductive.
Report R1 and full-night sensitivity together. Do not choose the better result as a new winner.

What the evidence does and does not show
The difference from R1 remains uncertain
A paired participant-level bootstrap uses 1,000 resamples with fixed seed 20261011.
The run misses the 71.86% interpretation threshold by only 0.024 points. That threshold was not blind to R1.
Thresholds preceded this run but followed baseline and R1 results. CI omits model-selection uncertainty.

Results vary across held-out folds
A headline average hides fold variability. R1 improves fold macro-F1 in all ten paired folds.
These plotted values pool the two test participants within each fold. They are not the headline subject mean.
Saved fold results only. Training sets overlap across folds, so folds are not independent samples.

N1 remains the hardest class
Per-class recall shows how many true epochs of each class the model recovers.
N1 remains the weakest class in both normalization runs, despite the overall improvement.
Pooled recall from archived test confusion matrices. Bar values are percentages.

Where R1's N1 errors go
The confusion matrix separates correct classifications from the direction of each error.
N1 errors spread across adjacent or competing stages. This describes mistakes, not their biological cause.
R1 pooled confusion counts. Cell intensity uses within-row percentages, not raw counts.

Rejected pilots and the next evidence gate
Small validation pilots did not pass
Three bounded validation-only pilots tested class balance, the classifier head and transition decoding.
None reached the required one-point macro-F1 gain with the other safeguards. We kept the original settings.
Validation deltas only, not new test gains. Head-only comparison uses its matched FP32 baseline.

Independent confirmation is not ready
A provenance audit separates known development exposure from participants with unresolved histories.
No participant cohort currently meets the evidence requirement for a certified independent evaluation.
Metadata-only audit. Availability is not proof of independence.

Limits on the scientific claim
R1 uses a single model seed and was selected after baseline test failures. Its confidence interval is conditional.
These results do not establish clinical validity, equivalence to another paper, or online performance.
Subject-wise protocol differs from the paper; test < 10 subjects per fold (20 total)

A useful result with a clear evidence boundary
The R1 package scored higher in this cohort. Normalization and retrained weights changed together.
The next scientific gate is a locked protocol and genuinely independent participants, after human approval.
Sleep-EDF Expanded 1.0.0. Kemp et al. 2000. Goldberger et al. 2000. ODC-By 1.0.
